title: Modern Angular Signals Architecture
exp: Angular 17+ introduced reactive Signals. Senior Angular roles expect deep knowledge of signal, computed, effect, linkedSignal, resource, input(), output(), and model().
pts: **`signal(initialValue)`:** reactive value container; write via `.set()` or `.update()`.
**`computed(() => ...)`:** memoized reactive computation; read-only; lazy evaluation.
**`effect(() => ...)`:** side-effect runner for DOM sync/logging; runs inside injection context.
**`linkedSignal` & `resource`** (Angular 19+): signals dependent on upstream inputs and async data fetching streams.
pr: Implement an async data resource using `resource()`

r: Deep mechanics of Modern Angular Signals Architecture under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: What is the key reactivity difference between RxJS Observables and Angular Signals?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** RxJS Observables represent push-based asynchronous streams of events over time. Signals represent pull-based synchronous reactive values that automatically track dependency graphs and memoize state changes without requiring explicit subscription management.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Angular Signals maintain an internal reactive dependency graph (ReactiveNode). When a signal value updates, it marks dependent computed nodes as stale without running change detection immediately. Evaluation happens lazily when read, updating only impacted DOM bindings.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Writing to signals inside an effect() can trigger infinite reactive loops or untracked state dependencies. Fix: use computed() or linkedSignal() for derived state sync, keeping effect() strictly for un-tracked side effects like logging or localStorage.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide fine-grained, synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require learning new primitives (input(), output(), model()) compared to classic RxJS BehaviorSubjects.

qa.q: Why should effects not be used for state synchronization in Angular Signals?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Using effects to update other signals causes cascading re-evaluations and potential cyclic dependencies. Use computed() or linkedSignal() for derived state synchronization.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Angular Signals maintain an internal reactive dependency graph (ReactiveNode).
